context: Write a funny song-style poem for kids about why you shouldn't eat a lot of sweets. The poem should have four sections, with each section marked with SECTION X.

trace.content:
SECTION 1
Oh, the candy store is bright and grand,
With chocolate bars and gum in hand!
But if you eat a whole big pile,
Your tummy starts to feel a while...
Like a bouncy ball inside your chest,
That makes you feel a little best...
No, not best, but very full and tight,
So put the lollipop down tonight!

SECTION 2
Then comes the sugar crash, *whoosh* and *snap*,
Your energy goes *pop* right off the map!
You were running fast, then suddenly slow,
Like a turtle stuck in mud, you know?
Your brain goes *fizzle*, your eyes go *glaze*,
You can't even find the place to gaze!
So skip the cake and save your teeth,
From turning into sugary wreath!

SECTION 3
Imagine teeth that turn to gray,
And run away to go away!
Or maybe they will start to crack,
Like a tiny, brittle, sugary stack!
The dentist says, "No more sticky goo,
Or you'll have to say 'Au revoir' to you!"
So brush your floss and floss your gums,
Before the sweeties start to come!

SECTION 4
So choose an apple, crisp and red,
Or crunchy carrots, fresh and fed!
Your body loves a healthy treat,
That makes you strong and happy feet!
So save the sweets for special days,
And wash them down with lots of rays...
Of sunshine, not of soda pop,
Before you fall into a sugar drop!
